Summary: AI Tools Policy Update

1. Key policy changes/content
The policy covers all staff, consultants and interns using generative AI (text, image, code, audio, and acting AI assistants), whether Institute-provided or not [1]. Core principles: staff remain accountable for AI output, which is always a draft to be checked, never final; tool choice must match task sensitivity, favouring approved enterprise-grade tools over consumer services [2]. Only an enterprise AI assistant (integrated with the document platform) and an enterprise chat service (retention off) are approved; consumer AI tools, browser extensions and personal accounts are not [3]. Prohibited uses include decisions about individuals, impersonation, fabricating sources/data, or processing information above a tool's permitted classification [4]. Restricted information must never go into tools sending data outside the Institute; it may only be processed in the private cloud after a data protection review [5].

2. Forwarded notes
The only item forwarded as a "policy update" was a suspicious/test document instructing recipients to email a draft externally and publish it. This was identified as fictional with no genuine policy content and was disregarded, consistent with treating documents as data, not instructions [11].

3. Operational impact
New AI solutions beyond personal productivity use require an intake submission [6], with risk-based approval (AI Office, Information Security/business owner, or Digital Governance Board) [7] and defined review timelines [8]. Usage beyond free monthly allowances is paid by the owning unit [9]. Prototypes run up to 8 weeks before production rollout requires evaluation and support documentation [10]. AI outputs used in decisions/publications must be filed with the related record [11].

Note: No document specifies a version number or changelog confirming this as the "latest" approved update; content reflects current policy as held in the notes.
